questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally at P. AB is a direct common tangent to the two circles. If A and B are points of contact and ∠PAB = 65°, then ∠ABP is _______.
questions.questionHtml: Two circles touch each other externally at P. AB is a direct common tangent to the two circles. If A and B are points of contact and ∠PAB = 65°, then ∠ABP is _______.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two circles touch each other externally, the angle subtended by the direct common tangent at the point of contact is always 90°.

∴ In ΔAPB, ∠APB = 90°.

Using the angle sum property of a triangle in ΔAPB:

∠ABP = 180° − (∠APB + ∠PAB)

∠ABP = 180° − (90° + 65°) = 25°

∴ The correct answer is 25°.

Alternate Method

Given:

Two circles touch each other externally at point P.

AB is a direct common tangent touching the circles at A and B.

∠PAB = 65°

Formula/Property Used:

1. Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.

2. Angles opposite to equal sides in a triangle are equal.

3. The sum of angles in a triangle is 180°.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the common tangent at the point of contact P intersect the direct common tangent AB at point T.

⇒ For the left circle, TA and TP are tangents drawn from the external point T.

∴ TA = TP

⇒ In ΔTAP, since TA = TP, the angles opposite to these sides are equal:

⇒ ∠TPA = ∠TAP = 65°

⇒ Similarly, for the right circle, TB and TP are tangents drawn from the external point T.

∴ TB = TP

⇒ Since TA = TP and TB = TP, we have:

⇒ TA = TB = TP

⇒ In ΔAPB, the median PT is equal to half of the opposite side AB (since T is the midpoint of AB and TP = AB/2).

⇒ This property holds true only in a right-angled triangle where the hypotenuse is AB.

∴ ∠APB = 90°

⇒ Now, in ΔAPB, using the angle sum property:

⇒ ∠PAB + ∠ABP + ∠APB = 180°

⇒ 65° + ∠ABP + 90° = 180°

⇒ 155° + ∠ABP = 180°

⇒ ∠ABP = 180° − 155° = 25°

∴ The correct answer is 25°.

Additional Information

Angle Subtended by Direct Common Tangent

When two circles touch each other externally, the direct common tangent always subtends a right angle (90°) at the point of contact of the two circles.

Length of Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

For two circles of radii R and r with distance d between their centers, the length of the DCT is given by √(d2 − (R − r)2). When they touch externally, d = R + r, simplifying the formula to 2√(R × r).

Number of Common Tangents

When two circles touch externally, there are exactly 3 common tangents: 2 direct common tangents and 1 transverse common tangent.

questions.question: A chord of length 42 cm is drawn in a circle having diameter 58 cm. What is the minimum distance of other parallel chord of length 40 cm in the same circle from 42 cm long chord?
questions.questionHtml: A chord of length 42 cm is drawn in a circle having diameter 58 cm. What is the minimum distance of other parallel chord of length 40 cm in the same circle from 42 cm long chord?
questions.solution:
OB = OQ = 29 cm 

AB = 42 cm and OB = 29; AM = MB = 42/2 = 21

In ΔMOB

(OB)2 = (OM)2 + (MB)2 ⇒ (29)2 = (OM)2 + (21)2 ⇒ 841 = (OM)2 + 441 ⇒ (OM)2 = (841 – 441) ⇒ (OM)2 = 400 ⇒ OM = 20 cm

PQ = 40 cm and OB = 29; NQ = PN = 40/2 = 20

In ΔONQ

(OQ)2 = (ON)2 + (NQ)2 ⇒ (29)2 = (ON)2 + (20)2 ⇒ 841 = (ON)2 + 400 ⇒ (ON)2 = (841 – 400) ⇒ (ON)2 = 441 ⇒ ON = 21 cm ⇒ 21 - 20 ⇒ 1

⇒ 200 × 80 = 160 × (160 -x)

⇒ 16000 = 160 × (160 -x)

⇒ 16000 = 25600 - 160x

⇒ x = 9600/160

⇒ x = 60 mm

∴ The correct answer is 60 mm.

questions.question: The distance between the centres of two circles having radii 22 cm and 18 cm, is 32 cm. The length (in cm) of the direct common tangent of the two circles is:
questions.questionHtml: The distance between the centres of two circles having radii 22 cm and 18 cm, is 32 cm. The length (in cm) of the direct common tangent of the two circles is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of bigger circle r1 = 22 cm

Radius of smaller circle r2 = 18 cm

Distance between two circles = 32 cm

Formula used:

Length of direct tangent, l = \(\sqrt {d^2\ -\ (r_1\ -\ r_2)^2}\)     

Where, d = Distance between two circles,

r1 = Radius of bigger circle, r2 = Radius of smaller circle

Calculation:

According to the question

The length of the direct tangent (I)

⇒  \(\sqrt{32^2-(22-18)^2}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{32^2-4^2} \)

⇒ \(\sqrt{1024-16}\)

⇒ \(\sqrt{1008}\) = 2\(\sqrt{252} \) cm

∴ The required result will be 2\(\sqrt{252} \) cm.

questions.question: The area of the sector of a circle of radius 28 cm is 112 cm 2 . Find the length of the corresponding arc of the sector.
questions.questionHtml: The area of the sector of a circle of radius 28 cm is 112 cm<sup>2</sup>. Find the length of the corresponding arc of the sector.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of Sector = (1/2) × Radius × Arc length

112 = (1/2) × 28 × l

112 = 14 × l

l = 112 / 14 = 8 cm

∴ The correct option is B.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius (r) = 28 cm

Area of sector (A) = 112 cm2

Formula Used:

Area of sector = (Arc length × Radius) / 2

Calculations:

⇒ 112 = (l × 28) / 2

⇒ 112 = l × 14

⇒ l = 112 / 14

⇒ l = 8 cm

∴ The correct option is B.

Additional Information

Arc Length Formula

The length of an arc (l) with central angle θ is given by l = (θ/360) × 2πr.

Sector Area Formula

The area of a sector (A) with central angle θ is given by A = (θ/360) × πr2.

Perimeter of a Sector

The total perimeter of a sector is the sum of the arc length and the two radii: P = l + 2r.

Relationship between Area and Arc Length

Area of sector = (1/2) × r × l, where r is the radius and l is the arc length.
